# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

name: INSIGHTS.md
text:
# INSIGHTS — summarized, verified findings (accumulate across the whole run)

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>
    - What worked (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - Promising but not yet tried:

## Reply-channel form (```python fence vs tool-call wrapper)
- What worked (confirmed by RESULT, `r1_contract`): a worked fenced example plus naming the exact wrapper tokens the model emits (`<|tool_call>`, `call:python_interpreter`, `<function_calls>`) as a *symptom* with its consequence ("nothing runs; after three such replies the task is abandoned with no output file"). 13-1 fixed in both screen and full val. 5/40 val tasks were failing this way with no output file at all — the cheapest cluster in the run.
- What didn't: n/a.
- Promising but not yet tried: nothing — treat this cluster as closed unless traces show it return.

## Grader contract (sheet identity + cell types)
- What worked (confirmed by RESULT, `r1_contract`): forbidding `DataFrame.to_excel`/`pd.ExcelWriter` for output_path **with the reasons stated**, paired with a worked `openpyxl.load_workbook(IN) → ws[a1] = v → wb.save(OUT)` recipe, and a "write values in their NATIVE Python type" rule. 44913 went 0→1 (it had every value correct and scored 0 on `worksheet not found`). Verified in source: `evaluation.py:cell_level_compare` returns `(False, "worksheet not found")` when the sheet name is absent, and `compare_cell_value` rejects `type(v1) != type(v2)`.
- What didn't: n/a.
- Promising but not yet tried: nothing further needed here.

## Preview coordinates
- What worked (confirmed by RESULT, `r1_contract`): "preview row i is Excel row i+2, pandas column j is Excel column j+1" — the adapter's `_spreadsheet_preview` itself annotates the extent as `rows 1-{nrows+1}` because pandas consumes row 1 as the header. Do not remove this.
- Promising but not yet tried: the preview's stated `data extent` can UNDERSTATE the workbook's own reference range (41978's extent said rows 1-185 while its own formulas span `$G$14:$G$9696`). Unresolved whether a rule about that helps or hurts.

## Verification that verifies nothing
- What worked (confirmed by RESULT, `r1_contract`): a copyable CHECK recipe that re-opens the SAVED file, addresses cells by literal A1 names (never by the write indices), prints sheetnames, and prints the EMPTY set and the CHANGED set; plus an explicit FINISH condition ("reply with no code block once CHECK is all-clear") and "never re-send an identical block" — without the latter, traces showed the same block re-sent 20–26 times.
- What didn't (confirmed by RESULT, `r1_contract`): the EMPTY/CHANGED recipe is a *presence and blast-radius* check, NOT a correctness check. 41978 printed `EMPTY: 0 []` / `CHANGED: 10 [...]` — exactly the expected shape — on a wrong answer, and was the round's only resolved regression. A CHECK needs at least one value-level reconciliation against a reference the agent did not compute itself.

## Criteria-value normalization (NEW cluster, opened by r1_contract's only regression)
- What didn't (confirmed by RESULT, `r1_contract`): 41978 regressed 1→0. It matched a filter criterion by the literal/type it assumed rather than the values actually present in the column (`int(y) == 2015` on the year column, while the workbook's own `=COUNTIF($G$14:$G$9696,"2015")` treats that column as TEXT). Seed and both control replicates used `str(y) == str(year)` plus `str(s).strip().lower() == 'open'` and scored 1.0. The agent even reasoned itself out of normalizing: "case-insensitive check usually safer, but instruction says 'open'".
- Promising but not yet tried: a rule to (a) print the DISTINCT values of any column you filter on before writing the comparison, (b) compare text criteria case- and whitespace-insensitively and numeric-looking criteria on both sides as strings, and (c) when the workbook contains its own equivalent computation (a formula, a summary column, a sample row), reproduce that number first and treat a disagreement as your bug. Note (c) already exists in prompt.md §3 as prose and was NOT exercised in 41978's trace — so the FORM (prose advice) is what failed, not the content; it needs to be a step in the CHECK recipe.

<!-- cap-evolve:insights-append-below -->

name: JOURNAL.md
text:
# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration r1_contract — fenced-reply contract (prompt.md) + workbook-preservation & re-derive-CHECK contract (task_template.md)
- Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
  - `prompt.md` §1 "Reply format": worked ```python example + the exact failure symptom named (`<|tool_call>`, `call:python_interpreter`, `<function_calls>`, XML/channel tags, bare unfenced code) with its consequence (nothing runs → 3 such replies abandons the task, no output file, score 0). Targets cluster 1 (FORM, 5/40 val).
  - `prompt.md` §2: ordered INSPECT → SOLVE → CHECK → FINISH, with FINISH defined as "reply with no code block once CHECK is all-clear". Targets the 20-26x identical-resend / never-terminates behaviour.
  - `prompt.md` §3: answer_position is a BOUNDARY not a quota (untouched cells inside it are graded and must keep their original value); the sheet must survive under its own name or the grader scores 0; literal values not formulas; NATIVE Python types (grader compares `type()`); a stated precision clause outranks a rounded inline example; preview row i = Excel row i+2 and pandas col j = Excel col j+1; a missed lookup is a bug not a blank; reconcile against the workbook's own worked example/summary column. Targets cluster 2 (CONTRACT/STRUCTURE, 10/40 val).
  - `prompt.md` §4: the CHECK block as a copyable recipe that re-derives by literal A1 names (sheetnames present, EMPTY set, CHANGED set) + "never re-send an identical block". Targets the "verification printed the bug and was read as success" sub-cluster.
  - `task_template.md`: field values moved to the top, then "What these fields mean" (incl. preview offset, `Unnamed: N` are real columns), then a worked openpyxl-load-assign-save recipe, an explicit prohibition on `DataFrame.to_excel`/`pd.ExcelWriter` for output_path WITH the four reasons (sheet renamed → grader finds no sheet, other sheets dropped, types changed, NaN cells blanked), `pd.read_excel(..., header=None, dtype=object, keep_default_na=False)` for reads, `ws.delete_cols/insert_rows` for structural edits, and the 3-step contract. All 7 placeholders preserved and verified via `.format()`.
  - `task_template.md`: replaced the old closing framing with "An output file existing is NOT being done — a wrong-but-present file is the most common way this task is failed."
- Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe:
  - Fence rule → the 5 val tasks abandoned with no output file (13-1 among them) produce a file at all. Safe: tasks already emitting fences see an example of what they already do.
  - to_excel prohibition → 44913 (every value correct, scored 0 on `"worksheet not found"`) passes. Blast radius audited: 11 passing tasks used `to_excel`; only 48924 was at risk (it passed only because pandas coerced strftime strings back to Timestamps) and the native-type clause is the correct fix for it per `evaluation.py:transform_value/compare_cell_value`.
  - answer_position-as-boundary → 341-40 (overwrote 955 cells whose gold was their own original content). Safe: it forbids writes, never requires new ones.
  - preview offset → 52807 (read row 4 for a row-5 header), 55817 (read A1:A35 for A2:A36). Verified against `adapter.py:_spreadsheet_preview`, which itself annotates `rows 1-{nrows+1}` with "pandas consumed row 1 as the header".
  - re-derive CHECK → 10 tasks whose verification output visibly contained the bug; 5835 (7 of 17 target cells left blank).
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — this is iteration 1; LEDGER/RUNMAP were baseline-only and there was no rejected.jsonl/history.jsonl.
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet measured.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: the 6 val tasks still failing (11842, 341-40, 38985, 49036, 535-20, 5835) and — newly surfaced by this round — **unnormalized text matching** (41978: the only resolved regression). 41978 has G14:G185 years vs J14:J185 statuses holding `Open`/`Closed`; the agent matched `s == 'Open'` after explicitly reasoning "case-insensitive check usually safer, but instruction says 'open'" — it took the instruction's lowercase quoting as the literal cell value. The seed and both control replicates used `str(s).strip().lower() == 'open'` and passed. My §3 "a stated precision/rendering clause holds even when an inline example looks rounded" plausibly reinforced treating the instruction's quoted string as authoritative over the observed cell. The CHECK block did run and printed clean, because it verifies presence/change, not correctness — a value-level cross-check against a workbook-internal reference is the missing piece.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first round, accepted: 0.625 → 0.775, Δ +0.10 vs bar 0.0784, verdict_stable true).
- Focus next iteration: a filter-value-normalization rule (match text criteria case/whitespace-insensitively against the values actually present in the column, which you must print first) plus a CHECK step that reconciles at least one computed number against a workbook-internal reference. Then the remaining 6.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.775 Δ=+0.150 · fixed={13-1, 44913, 48608, 52807, 55468, 55817, 56920} · broke={41978} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).
<!-- r1_contract: ACCEPTED val=0.775 Δ=+0.150 -->

name: LEDGER.md
text:
# LEDGER — factual run record (framework-maintained; READ-ONLY)

The measured record of every iteration: which candidate, its parent, whether the gate ACCEPTED it, the val reward + Δ, and the tasks it broke / fixed. Facts only — your own narrative, lessons, and refuted hypotheses go in JOURNAL.md. Use this to never re-introduce a change that broke a task, and to see which approaches the gate accepted vs rejected.

`broke` / `fixed` list only tasks whose move EXCEEDED 2·SE of its own per-task measurement error, so they are claims the measurement can support. A task that moved by less is in `unresolved`: it is NOT evidence the edit did anything to that task, in either direction, and must not be reasoned about as a regression or a win. Do not redesign an edit because a task appears there — re-measure it, or ignore it.

## Iterations
| iter | candidate | parent | outcome | val | Δ vs parent | broke (were passing) | fixed | unresolved (moved < 2·SE) |

| 1 | r1_contract | seed | ACCEPT | 0.775 | +0.150 | {41978} | {13-1, 44913, 48608, 52807, 55468, 55817, 56920} | {} |

## Current best: r1_contract

name: META_INSIGHTS.md
text:
# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration r1_contract (round 1)
- Strategy tried, and whether it moved val: audit the measurement surface FIRST (free — confirmed no infra cluster, and that train/val cluster signatures overlap), then cluster the traces by root cause with two parallel read-only subagents, then read the adapter + grader source to turn each cluster into a *verified* mechanism rather than a guess, then edit BOTH capability files in one candidate (prompt.md = reply channel + reasoning order; task_template.md = field semantics + output mechanics), screen 13 ids to triage, then gate on full val. Moved val 0.625 → 0.775, Δ +0.10 vs bar 0.0784, verdict_stable. LEDGER row: iter 1.
- What made the difference: every rule was traced to a line of read-only source (`_extract_python`, the `no_code_replies >= 3` break, `cell_level_compare`'s `worksheet not found`, `compare_cell_value`'s type check, `_spreadsheet_preview`'s `nrows+1`), so the edits were mechanisms, not style. Also: checking the blast radius BEFORE spending the round (11 passing tasks used `to_excel`; only 48924 was at risk, and reading `transform_value` showed the native-type clause covers it).
- Plateau/stall signal: none yet (round 1 accepted). Screen-before-gate cost ~3.5 min and correctly predicted the accept — keep it as the default triage step.
- What to try next iteration: the round's one resolved regression (41978) shows the real lever for round 2 — **prose advice in prompt.md §3 that the trace shows was never exercised means the FORM was wrong, not the content**. The "reproduce the workbook's own worked example first" rule existed as prose and was skipped; it needs to become a numbered step inside the CHECK recipe. Generalize: when a cluster survives an edit, first ask whether the agent ever ran the rule before rewriting what the rule says.
- Also worth noting for pacing: 1 full-val gate at concurrency 8 ≈ 36 min wall clock, so ~8 rounds is the real budget ceiling and siblings must be screened, not gated.

name: PROCESS.md
text:
# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Iteration: `r1_contract` (round 1), parent `seed`. Gate: full val (n=40), paired, k_se 1.0, `--gate-against control`, concurrency 8, 1 trial.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | CONTRACT/STRUCTURE — "wrong-but-present output file" | 10/40 val (incl. 44913, 341-40, 52807, 55817, 5835, 48924-adjacent) | agent produces a file that violates the grader's contract: pandas rebuild renames the sheet (`cell_level_compare` → `(False, "worksheet not found")`), `type(v1) != type(v2)` mismatches, cells inside answer_position overwritten though their gold was their own original content, preview off-by-one carried into a write, silently-swallowed lookup misses | KNOWLEDGE | rewrite task_template.md: worked openpyxl load→assign→save recipe, to_excel prohibition with reasons, field semantics incl. preview offset |
| 2 | FORM — reply never executes | 5/40 val (incl. 13-1) | model emits `<|tool_call>call:python_interpreter …` / XML / bare code instead of a ```python fence → `_extract_python` returns None → `_NO_CODE_REMINDER` → 3 such replies breaks the loop with NO output file, score 0 | BEHAVIORAL | prompt.md §1: worked fenced example + prohibition naming the exact wrapper tokens as the symptom |
| 3 | VERIFICATION theatre | ~10/40 val (overlaps 1) | agent "verifies" by printing what it just wrote, by the same indices it wrote with; output visibly contained the bug (leading `None`, 12 identical numbers, 7 NaNs in a 17-cell target) and was read as success. Also: identical code block re-sent 20–26× (no termination rule) | BEHAVIORAL | prompt.md §4: copyable CHECK recipe addressing literal A1 names; EMPTY/CHANGED sets; explicit FINISH condition; never re-send an identical block |
| 4 | INSTRUCTION-CLAUSE DROP | 2/40 val (49036, others) | an explicit precision/duplicate/pairing clause late in the instruction is discarded in favour of a rounded inline example | KNOWLEDGE | prompt.md §3 precision clause |

Measurement audit done first (free): no `_sandbox_access_denied` / mount / PermissionError cluster; every rollout has a trace and a real score, so these are capability failures, not infrastructure. Train and val cluster signatures overlap, so train-driven edits can move val.

## Changes made this iteration
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 (FORM) | prohibition + preceding symptom | prompt.md §1 | worked ```python example; names the wrapper tokens the model actually emits and the consequence (nothing runs, 3 strikes = abandoned). Generalizes: it is about the reply channel, independent of task content | yes — tasks already fencing correctly just see an example of what they do |
| 3 | positive recipe + termination rule | prompt.md §2, §4 | ordered INSPECT→SOLVE→CHECK→FINISH; CHECK re-derives by literal A1 names and prints EMPTY/CHANGED; "never re-send an identical block"; FINISH = no code block once clean | yes — adds a step, changes no computation |
| 1 | structural REQUIRED slot + prohibition with reasons | task_template.md | openpyxl load→assign→save as the canonical output path; `to_excel`/`ExcelWriter` forbidden for output_path with the 4 concrete consequences; `pd.read_excel(header=None, dtype=object, keep_default_na=False)` for reads; `ws.delete_cols/insert_rows` for structural edits | audited below |
| 1 | field semantics | task_template.md + prompt.md §3 | answer_position = boundary not quota; sheet must survive by name; native Python types; preview row i = Excel row i+2, pandas col j = Excel col j+1; `Unnamed: N` are real columns; a missed lookup is a bug not a blank | yes — all are constraints on writes, none demand new writes |
| 4 | conditional on an observable predicate | prompt.md §3 | if the instruction states a precision/rendering, it holds even when an inline example looks rounded — satisfy both | yes |

## Verify-the-fix
- **13-1 and the 4 other FORM tasks** (trace: replies of the form `<|tool_call>call:python_interpreter{"code": …}`, three of them, then loop break, no output file) → §1 now shows the fence and names those exact tokens as "you have already failed". Screen result: 13-1 fixed. Full-val: 13-1 fixed vs both control replicates.
- **44913** (trace: `df.to_excel(output_path, index=False)`; score feedback `worksheet not found`; every value in the frame correct) → task_template now forbids `to_excel` for output_path and shows `openpyxl.load_workbook(IN) … wb.save(OUT)`. Full-val: 44913 fixed vs both controls.
- **341-40** (trace: wrote a computed value into all 955 cells of a large answer_position; gold for most of them was their own original content) → "answer_position is the boundary of what you may change, not a quota to fill" + the CHANGED-set CHECK, which would have printed 955 changed cells for a 40-cell instruction.
- **52807 / 55817** (traces: read preview row 4 as Excel row 4 for a row-5 header; read A1:A35 for a stated A2:A36) → preview-offset rule, verified against `adapter.py:_spreadsheet_preview`, which annotates the extent as `rows 1-{nrows+1}` precisely because pandas ate row 1 as the header.
- **5835** (trace: 7 of 17 target cells left blank by a lookup inside `except: continue`) → "a computation that yields nothing for a cell is a BUG to find, not a blank to write. Print the unmatched key" + the EMPTY-set CHECK.
- **48924 blast radius** (a PASSING task that used `to_excel`): it passed only because pandas coerced its strftime strings back to Timestamps. `evaluation.py:transform_value` sends `datetime` → Excel serial float and `compare_cell_value` rejects `type(v1) != type(v2)`, so the native-type clause in §3 is the correct replacement mechanism, not a gamble. The other 10 passing `to_excel` tasks write single-sheet frames whose values and types are unaffected by switching to openpyxl-in-place.
- **297-42** flagged as second-order (hand-indexed 821×15 write) — no edit targets it.
- Pre-gate mechanical verification: `_task_template_error` → None; `.format()` renders 4428 chars with every placeholder bound; `system-prompt/scripts/run.py --baseline candidates/seed` → `problems: []`, `warnings: []` (no rule loss).

## Measured outcome (for the next iteration to build on)
- Screen (13 ids, 3m21s): Δ̄ +0.3077, SE 0.1332, `regressed: []`, `fixed: [13-1, 53647, 55468, 56920]`, `promote`.
- Full val: r1_contract **0.775** vs controls 0.675 / 0.625. gate_delta **+0.10** vs threshold **0.0784**. `verdict: accept`, `verdict_stable: true`. noise floor 0.05.
- FIXED vs BOTH control replicates: 13-1, 44913, 48921, 55468, 56920. BROKE: **41978 only** (46646 and 53647 each passed in one control replicate and failed in the other → inside the noise band, not resolved regressions; per LEDGER's own rule they must not be reasoned about as regressions).
- **41978 root cause, read from the trace (this is the finding to carry forward):** the workbook holds `Open`/`Closed` in J14:J185; the instruction says «count if the corresponding cells from J14 to J185 are marked as 'open'». The agent's own INSPECT printed `Row 15: G=2021, J=Open`, and it then wrote in a comment "case-insensitive check usually safer, **but instruction says 'open'**" and matched `s == 'Open'`. That part was right; the LOWER-than-expected counts come from the year side — it compared `int(y) == year` against the year values while the workbook's own H2:H11 formulas read `=COUNTIF($G$14:$G$9696,"2015")`, i.e. the file's own reference counts the same column as TEXT over a wider range. Seed/controls used `str(y) == str(year)` + `str(s).strip().lower() == 'open'` and scored 1.0. So the cluster is **criteria-value normalization**: matching a filter criterion by an assumed literal/type instead of by the values actually present in the column. Its CHECK passed because the recipe verifies presence and change-set, not value correctness.

## Process & features used
- Serial driving with two parallel read-only subagents for trace clustering (one on val, one on train), plus a screen pass before the full-val gate.
- Prior iterations read from ./prior_iterations/ + ./RUNMAP.md: none exist — this is iteration 1 (LEDGER baseline-only, no rejected.jsonl/history.jsonl).
- Read as ground truth (never edited): `adapters/adapter.py` (`_FENCE_RE`, `_extract_python`, `_NO_CODE_REMINDER`, the `no_code_replies >= 3` break, `_TEMPLATE_REQUIRED/_OPTIONAL`, `_task_template_error`, `_spreadsheet_preview`), `third_party/spreadsheetbench/evaluation/evaluation.py` (`transform_value`, `compare_cell_value`, `cell_level_compare`), `third_party/spreadsheetbench/inference/code_exec.py` (`extract_code`).

## Good things to PRESERVE
- The fenced-reply section with the wrapper tokens named as a symptom — it is the cheapest fix in the run (5 val tasks had NO output file at all).
- The to_excel prohibition WITH its four reasons, and the native-Python-type rule that makes it safe for 48924.
- The preview-offset arithmetic (verified against the adapter's own preview annotation — do not "simplify" it away).
- The explicit FINISH condition; without it the agent re-sent identical blocks 20–26 times.
- The CHECK recipe's EMPTY/CHANGED sets — but note they are NOT a correctness check (41978 shows a clean CHECK on a wrong answer). Extend it; do not delete it.

## Deliberately skipped
- Infra/noise: none found — the measurement audit showed no sandbox/mount failure cluster, so nothing was written off as infra.
- 46646, 53647: moved inside the noise band (each passed in one control replicate and failed in the other). Per LEDGER's rule they are `unresolved`, not regressions; no edit was designed against them.
- 297-42: second-order (hand-indexed 821×15 write) — not a cluster, one task.
- Writing formula strings: no trace showed the agent emitting live formulas into answer_position, so the "prefer literals" rule was kept as cheap insurance rather than expanded.

name: prompt.md
text:
You are a spreadsheet expert. You solve spreadsheet tasks by writing Python code that is executed
for you in a sandbox, one code block per round. You are graded ONLY on the cell values in the saved
output file — never on your explanation.

# 1. Reply format — this is what makes your code run

Every reply is exactly ONE fenced Python block and nothing else. The opening fence is the three
backtick characters followed immediately by the word `python`:

```python
import openpyxl
wb = openpyxl.load_workbook('/mnt/data/spreadsheet/EXAMPLE/1_EXAMPLE_init.xlsx')
print(wb.sheetnames)
```

Only text inside that fence is executed. There is no tool to call here — the fenced block IS the
interface. If you are about to reply with a tool-call wrapper (`<|tool_call>`,
`call:python_interpreter`, `<function_calls>`), with XML or channel tags, or with bare code and no
fence, then you have already failed: NOTHING runs, the round is wasted, and after three such replies
the task is abandoned with no output file and a score of zero.

One block per reply — if you write several, only the first one runs. Never write down what you think
the execution result will be: only the text the sandbox returns to you is real.

# 2. Work in this order

1. **INSPECT.** Load the workbook and print the actual cells you will read from and write to,
   addressed by real Excel coordinates. Confirm your anchors (header row, key column, first data
   row) hold what you expect before computing anything.
2. **SOLVE.** Compute the values and save the workbook to output_path.
3. **CHECK.** Run the verification block in section 4.
4. **FINISH.** Only once the CHECK prints all-clear, reply with no code block at all. That ends the
   task. Do not keep writing code after a clean CHECK.

# 3. What to write, and where

- `answer_position` is the boundary of what you may change, not a quota to fill. A cell inside it
  that the instruction does not ask you to compute must keep its ORIGINAL value — the grader
  compares every cell in the range, and counts an overwritten one as wrong. Never write outside
  `answer_position`.
- The sheet named in `answer_position` must still exist in the output file, under that same name;
  if `answer_position` names no sheet, the first sheet's name must be unchanged. The grader looks
  the sheet up BY NAME and scores zero when it is absent — a saved file whose sheet got renamed
  fails even when every value in it is correct.
- Write literal computed values, not live spreadsheet formulas: a formula string is compared as
  text and will not match.
- Write each value in its NATIVE Python type — `int`/`float` for numbers, a `datetime`/`date`
  object for dates, `str` only for genuine text. The grader compares types as well as values, so
  the text `"2021-12-04"` does not match a real date cell.
- If the instruction states a precision or rendering ("two decimals", "as a percentage", "as an
  integer"), that requirement holds even when an inline example looks rounded. Satisfy both: match
  the example's wording AND the stated precision.
- The preview you are given was produced by pandas with row 1 consumed as the header, and its row
  labels are 0-based. So preview row `i` is Excel row `i + 2`, and pandas column position `j` is
  Excel column `j + 1`. Do not carry a preview offset into a write — convert the letters in
  `answer_position` with `openpyxl.utils.column_index_from_string` and print the cell you are about
  to use to confirm it holds what you expect.
- If a computation yields nothing for a cell (a lookup missed, a key is absent), that is a BUG to
  find, not a blank to write. Print the unmatched key rather than swallowing it in
  `except: continue`.
- When the workbook already contains a worked example of the answer — a pre-filled sample row
  inside the target range, or a summary column computed the same way — reproduce it with your own
  code first. If your number disagrees with the workbook's own, your logic is wrong, not the file's.

# 4. The CHECK block — re-derive, do not just print

Printing the values you wrote proves nothing. The most common way to fail here is a check whose
output visibly contained the bug — a leading `None`, twelve identical numbers, seven `NaN`s in a
17-cell target — and was read as success. So address cells by their literal A1 names, never by the
same row/column index you used to write:

```python

ws_out = openpyxl.load_workbook(OUTPUT_PATH)[SHEET]   # SHEET from answer_position
ws_in  = openpyxl.load_workbook(INPUT_PATH)[SHEET]
print("sheets out:", openpyxl.load_workbook(OUTPUT_PATH).sheetnames)   # SHEET must be present

cells = ["F2", "F3", "F4", "F5"]        # every cell of answer_position, as literal A1 names
for a1 in cells[:40]:                   # for a big range, print the first 40 and count the rest
    print(a1, repr(ws_out[a1].value), type(ws_out[a1].value).__name__)

empty = [a1 for a1 in cells if ws_out[a1].value in (None, "")]
moved = [a1 for a1 in cells if ws_out[a1].value != ws_in[a1].value]
print("EMPTY:", len(empty), empty[:20])   # only cells meant to be empty may appear
print("CHANGED:", len(moved), moved[:20]) # must be exactly the cells the instruction asked for
```

Read that output against the instruction and against the preview you were given: a value that
contradicts a number visible in the preview is wrong even though it printed without error. If any
line is wrong, your next block must be DIAGNOSTIC — print the source cells and the intermediate
lookups — followed by a corrected write.

Never re-send a code block identical to one you already ran. If you are about to repeat yourself you
have stopped making progress, and the information you need is in cells you have not printed yet.

## What these fields mean

- **instruction** — the change to make. Read it to the end: a clause about how to treat duplicates,
  which rows pair up, or what precision to use is part of the requirement, not commentary.
- **spreadsheet_path** — the input workbook. Read it; never modify it in place.
- **spreadsheet_content** — the target range's size, each sheet's real data extent, and a pandas
  preview of the first rows. In that preview the leftmost column is a 0-based pandas index and row 1
  of the sheet was consumed as the header, so **preview row `i` is Excel row `i + 2`**, and pandas
  column position `j` is Excel column `j + 1`. Columns shown as `Unnamed: N` are real columns whose
  header cell is blank — not columns to skip. The data extent is authoritative; the preview is
  truncated.
- **instruction_type** — `Cell-Level Manipulation`: answer_position is the exact cell(s).
  `Sheet-Level Manipulation`: answer_position is the MAXIMUM range you may modify.
- **answer_position** — the only cells you may change. Every cell in it is graded, including the
  ones the instruction does not ask about: those must still hold their original value.
- **output_path** — write the finished workbook here, at exactly this path, creating parent
  directories if needed.

## How to produce the output file

The output must be the INPUT workbook with the required cells changed — same sheets, same sheet
names, everything else untouched. The reliable way is to load it with openpyxl, assign the target
cells, and save:

```python
import os, openpyxl
IN  = "{spreadsheet_path}"
OUT = "{output_path}"
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(OUT), exist_ok=True)

wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(IN)      # keeps every sheet, name and untouched cell
ws = wb["SheetNameFromAnswerPosition"]   # or wb[wb.sheetnames[0]] if answer_position names no sheet
ws["F2"] = 42                        # assign ONLY the cells the instruction asks for
wb.save(OUT)
```

You may use pandas to READ and compute. Do not use `DataFrame.to_excel` or `pd.ExcelWriter` to
produce output_path: that rebuilds the file from the frame rather than editing the original, which
renames the sheet (the grader then finds no sheet by that name and scores 0), drops the other
sheets, changes cell types, and blanks every cell pandas parsed as `NaN` — including cells whose
correct answer was their own original content. If you do read with pandas, prefer
`pd.read_excel(path, header=None, dtype=object, keep_default_na=False)` so literal text such as
`NA`, `None` or `-` is not silently turned into a blank.

For a structural change (deleting, inserting, or moving rows/columns) use openpyxl's
`ws.delete_cols`, `ws.insert_rows` and friends on the loaded workbook, not a pandas round-trip.

2. **SOLVE** — compute the values and save the workbook to output_path.
3. **CHECK** — re-open the SAVED file and verify it, addressing cells by literal A1 names rather

that ends the task. If the CHECK shows a problem, the next block must be diagnostic (print the source
